chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Shihab ibn Abdi Rabbihi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The deranged one who does not know how to divorce properly, his guardian divorces on his behalf according to the Sunnah.' I said, 'And if he was ignorant and divorced her three times in one sitting?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is returned to the Sunnah. So when three months or three menstrual periods have passed, she has been irrevocably divorced from him by one (divorce).'

key_terms.الْمَعْتُوهُ: The deranged or mentally unstable person who is not fully competent but not completely insane.
key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She has been irrevocably divorced from him.
key_terms.عَلَى السُّنَّةِ: According to the standard prophetic tradition/procedure.
key_terms.قُرُوءٍ: Menstrual periods (used here to measure the waiting period).
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: His guardian, who acts on his behalf in legal matters.
key_terms.يُرَدُّ إِلَى السُّنَّةِ: He is returned to the Sunnah (i.e., treated as if he followed the standard single divorce procedure).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the divorce of a mentally unstable person who divorces his wife three times at once?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'ghayr mukallaf' (non-competent) individuals, establishing that their guardian acts as their proxy in divorce to ensure legal validity. It specifically addresses the 'three divorces in one sitting' scenario, ruling it as a single revocable divorce (raj'i) rather than the final separation (ba'in) applied to competent adults, thereby protecting the wife from immediate irrevocability. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on intent and competence, linking the procedural delay to the waiting period (iddah) mentioned in the Quran.
